item.title: Netanyahu's office denies connection to election day arrests: 'False report'
item.description:
The Prime Minister’s Office rejected allegations in the Channel 12 report that Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's associates supplied information that led to the arrest of Ra’am activists, calling it a “false report" intended, it claimed, to suppress the election interference affair.
“Another false report packaged with dramatic music, as part of the serious attempts to silence the election interference affair. As for the facts: Information concerning criminal activity reached chief of staff Ido Norden. He fulfilled his duty, as expected of any law-abiding citizen, and put the individual in contact with the police. Any additional involvement by the chief of staff alleged in the report is false and constitutes grounds for a defamation lawsuit. He never spoke with police intelligence officials or other officials involved in the investigation. As Israeli citizens and the chief of staff learned through the media on election morning, a person was indeed caught with tens of thousands of shekels in cash and Ra’am ballot slips," Netanyahu’s office stated.

item.title: Report: Jensen Huang weighs return as Nvidia CEO
item.description:
Days after resigning, Nvidia’s co-founder is discussing a potential comeback with allies as prominent investors push the board to consider his return.
Nvidia co-founder Jensen Huang is considering returning as the company’s chief executive just days after his resignation, the Financial Times reported Sunday.
According to the report, Huang has discussed a potential comeback with allies in Silicon Valley who are seeking to persuade Nvidia’s board to reinstate him and secure support from the White House.
Nvidia shareholders Brad Gerstner, founder of Altimeter Capital, and Gavin Baker, head of Atreides Management, have urged the board to take a measured approach to choosing the company’s next leader and keep Huang’s potential return among its options.
Elon Musk has also backed calls for Huang’s reinstatement. Chief Financial Officer Colette Kress is currently serving as interim CEO.

item.title: Netanyahu at Unity Tent: We will work to all lengths to achieve unity
item.description:
Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu visited the Unity Tent MK Elisha Medan set up outside the Knesset in Jerusalem on Sunday.
During the visit, Medan told Netanyahu about his decision to erect the tent, the many visitors who came from across the country and from across the political spectrum, and the meetings that had taken place there.
Netanyahu expressed his support for Medan and praised him for his initiative and efforts to promote unity among the Israeli people. The two agreed that unity is an urgent necessity and pledged to work together in every possible way to achieve it.
